corrections.new: All silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility.
corrections.reason: Mill's exact quote in On Liberty is 'All silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility', not 'the opinion'.

quiz.q: Why does Mill's distinction between higher and lower pleasures make Bentham's felicific calculus unworkable?
options: Pleasures can now be measured purely by their duration and intensity rather than subjective feeling.
Qualitative differences in pleasures cannot be mathematically quantified or measured on a single numerical scale.
The state must decide the numerical value of intellectual happiness for all citizens equally.
Physical appetite provides greater quantifiable satisfaction to the soul than intellectual contemplation does.
quiz.why: Bentham assumed pleasure is purely quantitative and measurable, but Mill introduced qualitative differences, making mathematical calculation of utility impossible.

quiz.q: Why does Mill assert that silencing even a single dissenting voice is never justified?
options: Because every opinion expressed by any individual is equally valid, scientifically verifiable, and objectively true.
Because minority opinions must always override majority decisions in modern constitutional democratic systems.
Because suppressing an opinion assumes infallibility and deprives society of discovering truth or correcting errors.
Because unrestrained public debate guarantees immediate social consensus without creating ideological conflict.
quiz.why: Silencing speech assumes infallibility, whereas open debate either reveals new truth or allows individuals to correct their mistaken opinions.

quiz.q: Why does Ernest Barker criticize J.S. Mill as a 'prophet of empty liberty'?
options: Because dividing actions into self-regarding and other-regarding is artificial and invites massive state intervention.
Because Mill completely rejected private property and championed an unconditional socialist welfare state.
Because Mill subordinated individual liberty entirely to the mathematical calculation of collective pleasure.
Because Mill denied freedom of speech to eccentric individuals and non-conformist minorities.
quiz.why: Barker argued that separating human actions into self-regarding and other-regarding is artificial, ultimately leaving little genuine scope for liberty.

quiz.q: Why is J.S. Mill characterized in political theory as a 'reluctant democrat'?
options: He believed direct democracy was inferior to absolute monarchy in all civilized European nations.
He opposed representative institutions because they inevitably protect the interests of the wealthy bourgeoisie.
He rejected constitutional government in favor of an unregulated free market without statutory laws.
He feared uneducated majority rule and advocated elitist restrictions like weighted voting for educated citizens.
quiz.why: Mill feared democracy turning into mobocracy or the tyranny of the majority, proposing aristocratic measures like weighted voting to safeguard governance.
